method: scripts/perf/container-lifecycle-split.sh, median of 3, strictly serial phases; no-op container isolates lifecycle, in-guest window bracketed by guest clock reads, total measured from the host
finding: CONTAINER LIFECYCLE DOMINATES. carrick's create+teardown is ~1.75 s - 7.7x the 228 ms workload window the fs campaign has been optimizing, and 89% of the total a user waits for. The in-guest ratio (17.5x) and the total-wall ratio (12.6x) are different numbers against different denominators; the fs-walk <=2x bar is unreachable on in-guest work alone because the lifecycle term is fixed cost.
attribution_pointer: target/perf/fswalk-amp6.raw: 45,005 host calls attributed to carrick-only (outside guest syscall service) - dominated by ~26k unlinkat (scratch teardown, O(files in image)) plus clonefileat seeding. sweep_orphans already proves deferred reclamation is safe.
next: attack lifecycle: defer/rename-aside teardown, and profile boot (image seed, guest mapping, dyld/self-reexec) - these move total wall, which is what users experience; in-guest work is now the smaller half

method: scripts/perf/container-lifecycle-split.sh, median of 3, serial phases, same box/image as the baseline record
hatch_control: CARRICK_FS_DEFERRED_TEARDOWN=0 restores the synchronous path: 1,701-3,503 ms no-op vs 547-785 ms armed (output-capturing parent)
mechanism: scratch reclamation renamed aside (O(1)) and handed to a detached /bin/rm -rf spawned via posix_spawn with stdio redirected to /dev/null; sweep_orphans reclaims any .carrick-reap-* a dead reaper left
trap_found: the reaper initially INHERITED carrick's stdio, so any output-capturing parent (the conformance harness, $(...), CI) blocked on the pipe until the unlink finished - the removed wall reappeared as carrick looking slow. posix_spawn_file_actions_addopen(/dev/null) for fds 0,1,2 fixes it; this is why the change was measured BOTH with and without capture.
next: pre-guest create is now the larger lifecycle half (~430 ms): image seed/clonefile, guest mapping, dyld self-reexec, DSR setup

method: clonefile of top-level cache children across a 4-thread scope, paired A/B via CARRICK_FS_PARALLEL_SEED with reaper QUIESCENCE between samples (back-to-back runs otherwise contend with the detached reaper and produce noise that looks like signal)
verdict: NULL - identical steady-state 430 ms both arms; code reverted unlanded per the no-neutral-knobs rule
interpretation: APFS serializes directory-clone NAMESPACE work inside a volume, so concurrency buys no overlap. clonefileat remains ~333 ms of the create phase; removing it needs the clone to not happen at all (serve reads from the shared cache tree as a read-only lower layer, copy-up on write) - a redesign that touches every trusted fast lane, not a knob.

method: /usr/bin/time -p, 3 samples, reaper-drained between carrick samples; docker unchanged
note: TOTAL-WALL ratios, the number a user experiences. Campaign start for the same command was ~3.3 s carrick vs ~0.16 s docker (~20x); it is now 3.8x. The in-guest window (225 ms vs 12 ms = 18.5x) and the total wall (3.8x) are different denominators - the lifecycle half is now nearly at the 2x bar (2.7x) while the in-guest half is not.
